22 lines. Returns sum(exactAmountsIn) as the BPT estimate — a flat 1:1 quote. This is the quote the pooler's slippage logic consumes, so slippage is structurally unmodellable locally.

cluster.note: THE ONLY story-073-aware script outside DeployMocks. Rewritten by c054833 and walked back twice by d241e61. It is the regression test for the streamer wiring: its index-1 mint reverts 'Uniboost: nudgeStreamer unset' if setNudgeStreamer was skipped. It now asserts on the NudgeStreamer (batchMinter, USDC) BUFFER, not the batch minter's balance — the old assertion would always read zero under streamer gating. It mirrors DeployMocks' MOCK_NUDGE_SPLIT=30 / MOCK_NUDGE_SIZE=25 / LOCAL_STREAM_DURATION=6h and asserts them against chain state as a drift check. Carries an important documented limitation: stream MAGNITUDES cannot be asserted inside a forge script (the simulation pass shares one timestamp; vm.rpc evm_increaseTime moves only the live node; vm.warp moves only the simulation), so accrual is verified out of band with cast rpc.

The live mainnet state DeployMocks now diverges from. It deploys NudgeRatchetDelayRelease at index 7 (which story 073 RETIRES) and NFTStakerDepletion V1 (where DeployMocks now ends on V2), and it sets NO setNudgeStreamer on the three Uniboosts — which DeployMocks:1525-1534 says is not optional (Uniboost._dispatch reverts on every index-1/2/3 mint without it). Best structural template for a mid-flight live-funds cutover: precondition asserts before every mutation, and the replaceDispatcher price/decimals reset lesson (setPrice/setGrowthFactor MUST follow replaceDispatcher).

The only mainnet script that deploys SYA + BatchNFTMinter + BalancerPoolerV2 together and performs an old->new handoff with on-chain introspection, per-step progress tracking and preview mode. ~34 wiring calls. It is the closest existing analogue of a full-stack differential mainnet deploy. NOT streamer-aware: it still calls setNudgeAddress/setNudgeSplit with no setNudgeStreamer, i.e. the pre-streamer SYA wiring, and its setBatchDonationSize is 10 vs the local 30.
Its NatSpec says it 'Mirrors Phase 3.7 of DeployMocks.s.sol' — the existing precedent for the DeployMocks->mainnet differential pattern, and the closest thing to a worked example.

observationsForAuditor: MOCK-VS-REAL PARTITION (the core question): 19 mocks stand in for mainnet dependencies; 39 real first-party Phoenix contracts are deployed unmodified from the submodule pins; 9 canonical third-party contracts (WETH9 + UniV2) are deployed from real creation bytecode; 6 rehearsal artifacts are deployed but untracked. Every Phoenix contract under audit is REAL. What is faked is exclusively the EXTERNAL surface: tokens, ERC4626 yield vaults, the Balancer V3 stack, the Sky PSM, the Curve USDe route.

The mocks that matter most for rehearsal fidelity are the three that model PRICE: MockBalancerRouter returns a flat sum-of-inputs BPT quote (22 lines), MockBalancerVault mints BPT 1:1 with no invariant, and MockAutoDOLA/MockAutoUSDC have no previewRedeem divergence, no fees and no withdrawal queue. Consequently the local chain cannot exhibit single-sided-add value loss, Balancer slippage, or the Tokemak previewRedeem behaviour that bricked the YS-swap suite (ledger YS-01). MockMarketAMMAdapter is the one mock that deliberately models loss, and only as a flat per-leg bps haircut.

MockKendu's no-fee, no-tax design is asserted by the deploy script's own fee-on-transfer probe (DeployMocks:1660-1664) precisely because NudgeStreamer.collectNudge credits buffer += amount UNCONDITIONALLY without measuring the received balance. The local mock therefore GUARANTEES the probe passes. If the real Kendu has any transfer tax, the local rehearsal is a structural false negative and the only guard is a deploy-script require that mainnet would also have to carry.

The Mock-prefix strip in extract-addresses.js erases the mock/real distinction from every downstream artifact. Nothing in local.json, addresses.ts, local-addresses.ts, the :3001 API, or the UI marks a mock as a mock.

The anvil-derived ContractAddresses interface type-gates the hand-maintained mainnet address book. A purely local mock addition (MockKendu) forced a zero-address placeholder into mainnet-addresses.ts. Any mainnet consumer resolving Kendu or NudgeStreamer today gets address(0).

Story 073's entire surface — NudgeStreamer, BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, NFTStakerDepletionV2, NFTStakerMigrator, and the six-donor setNudgeStreamer fan-out — has NO mainnet counterpart. DeployMocks.s.sol:62 names it 'the streamer-era contract set (mirrors the mainnet cutover PLANNED in story 072)'.

Every dispatch path is now hard-gated on nudgeStreamer != 0. On the BalancerPoolerV2 index-4 path specifically the revert is SWALLOWED by _dispatch's try/catch, so a missed setNudgeStreamer on mainnet would produce a succeeding mint with a silently vanished donation — the same class as yield-claim-nft M-04 (unwired-hook zero-debt footgun).

The SYA setRewardToken ordering guard (D-10) is a deploy-script CONVENTION, not a contract invariant. It sidesteps ledger finding 0xd62cbfe8 (SYA run-14) by ordering alone; any post-deploy reward-token change on a live SYA re-arms the brick.

DeployMocks has NO block.chainid guard, unlike all seven DeployMainnet* scripts (which each carry require(block.chainid == 1) twice). The un-gated path contains unrestricted mock mints, two un-revoked phUSD.setMinter(deployer, true) grants, and the whole migration rehearsal. The project's own CLAUDE.md forbids exactly this.

The migration rehearsal leaves each of the three V1 stakers paused, unregistered from the global Pauser, with its pauser repointed to the deployer, and holding a stranded 10% of the reward budget — and none of the three V1 stakers or the three migrators is tracked, so they are invisible to progress.31337.json and the UI.
The author explicitly disclaims what the rehearsal proves: ORDERING (settle+freeze before moving the budget) is the finding story 072 must apply; SIZING is NOT solved and is inherited as OPEN.
